ai.description: Daboia russelii reaches 1.2–1.5m. It is light brown with three rows of dark, white-bordered oval spots. A distinct triangular head mark and loud, persistent hissing identify this species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Daboia russelii* is the three longitudinal rows of prominent, dark-brown, oval-shaped spots, each edged with a distinct black and white border.
ai.habitat: *Daboia russelii* inhabits open grasslands, scrublands, and agricultural fields across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 3,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: When threatened, *Daboia russelii* typically coils into an S-shape and emits a distinct, loud, and continuous hiss that sounds remarkably like a pressure cooker.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Daboia russelii* is ovoviviparous, typically breeding between spring and autumn. Females produce large litters of 20–40 live young, though up to 70 have been recorded.
ai.distributionRemarks: Daboia russelii is widely distributed across India, from the plains up to 2,500m, inhabiting diverse regions including the Deccan Plateau, Gangetic plains, and coasts.
